report.summary:
I repaired the cdme-accounting verifier and changed no test. Nothing was run, so the repaired result is not observed and nothing here claims the suite now passes.

Cause of the three failures in result 4279d0c9 (UAT-ACCT-NEG at AccountingVerifierSpec.scala:113, UAT-ACCT-BND at :122, UAT-ACCT-INV at :145): `AccountingVerifier.verify` returned Balanced whenever `difference >= 0L`. Any ledger with more input than output plus error sink therefore passed. The run shows this directly: (5,4,0) and (1,0,0) came back Balanced. That line is exactly the planned ACCOUNTING×NEG mutant listed in design/test-design.md §7 ("`== 0L` becomes `>= 0L`"). Before the edit the file's sha256 was 7ff8d8b7…; the repair schedule (§3, row M7) and test-design.md both record 56c2c1a1….

Fix: one line in `build_tenants/scala_spark/cdme-accounting/src/main/scala/com/cdme/accounting/AccountingVerifier.scala:40`, changed to `if (sum.difference == 0L) Balanced(sum) else Unbalanced(sum, sum.difference)`. This is the rule module-design §5.5 and implementation-design state:
- Balanced only when Σinput == Σoutput + ΣerrorSink, compared exactly, so ±1 is Unbalanced.
- Empty and all-zero ledgers give Balanced with zero totals.
- The verdict does not depend on entry order; the unchanged `foldLeft` in `totals` already sums per partition.

The file's digest is now 56c2c1a1df362be1…a470b, matching both records, and all 22 subject files match the schedule's §3 table (checked with `shasum -c`).

What did not change:
- The cdme-core DTOs (AccountingLedger, LedgerEntry, LedgerPartition, ExecutionResult) and the core-only dependency rule.
- The cdme-engine call site (`CdmeEngineImpl.accountStage` still matches `Balanced(_)` and `Unbalanced(_, difference)`).
- build.sbt, project files and module structure.
- AccountingVerifierSpec. Its assertions follow the requirement and test-design §5.5, so no test was defective.

I also rewrote `repair/component-repair-application.md`. It now records the observed failure from 4279d0c9 (command, environment, exit 1, the three verbatim assertion messages, report digests), the diagnosis, the before/after diff and digests, the unchanged seams and the open items. The file it replaced (sha256 07c1c38c…) said no repair was applied.

I did not run `sbt`, `scalac` or any Testing command, created no `target/` directory or scratch files, and wrote nothing outside the write scope. The only files written are the one-line source fix and the repair-application file.
